MRN estimator (marginal Radon–Nikodym weights)

Source: R/methods.R
mrn.Rd

Linear-weighted Hajek estimator using the marginal Radon–Nikodym identification weights (Proposition examples_of_weights (i)). Returns all well-defined causal effects and population average potential outcomes with variance estimates. The variance estimator is the Loewner-max HAC estimator \(\hat\Sigma_1\) (Theorem var_1) under cluster-level Bernoulli randomization, and the bias-corrected estimator \(\hat\Sigma_1^{bc}\) (Section 6.3) under complete randomization.

Usage

mrn(
  A,
  C,
  Y,
  W_C,
  W_Y,
  dist1 = "binom",
  params1 = list(prob = 0.5),
  dist0 = "binom",
  params0 = list(prob = 0),
  distC = "binom",
  paramsC = list(prob = 0.7),
  unit_weights = NULL,
  design = NULL
)

Arguments

A

n_unit x n_unit adjacency matrix of the interference network (with self-loops, as used throughout the project).

C

integer vector of length n_unit giving each unit's cluster id.

Y

numeric vector of observed outcomes (length n_unit).

W_C

0/1 vector of cluster-level treatments, indexed by cluster id.

W_Y

0/1 vector of individual-level treatments (length n_unit).

dist1, params1

within-cluster assignment law of the treated regime phi_1.

dist0, params0

within-cluster assignment law of the control regime phi_0.

distC, paramsC

cluster-level assignment law.

unit_weights

optional per-unit weights u_i = g_i / N_i (default: uniform 1 / n_unit).

design

optional override, "bernoulli" or "complete"; inferred from distC when NULL.

Value

A list with causal_effects, potential_outcomes (data frames of estimates / variances / standard errors), the estimand covariance matrix Sigma, and the chosen variance_type.

Examples

## Small geometric cluster network (a scaled-down version of the
## simulation pipeline in data_generation.R): units live around ten
## cluster centres and interfere with all units within distance 1.5.
set.seed(1)
n_per <- 6; K <- 10; n <- n_per * K
C <- rep(seq_len(K), each = n_per)                      # cluster ids
centers <- cbind(rep(1:5, 2), rep(1:2, each = 5)) * 4   # cluster centres
loc <- centers[C, ] + matrix(runif(2 * n, -1, 1), n, 2) # unit locations
A <- Matrix::Matrix(as.matrix(dist(loc)) <= 1.5, sparse = TRUE) * 1

## Two-stage assignment: clusters are treated w.p. 0.7 (cluster-level
## Bernoulli law distC); units in treated clusters get W = 1 w.p. 0.5
## (regime phi_1), units in control clusters w.p. 0.2 (regime phi_0).
W_C <- rbinom(K, 1, 0.7)
W_Y <- rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(W_C[C] == 1, 0.5, 0.2))

## Outcomes with neighbourhood interference (spillover beta = 2 from
## treated neighbours plus interaction gamma = 1 for treated units).
Y <- as.vector(-1 + A %*% (2 * W_Y) +
                 W_Y * as.vector(A %*% (1 * W_Y)) + rnorm(n))

## MRN estimator under cluster-level Bernoulli randomization:
## variance is the Loewner-max HAC estimator (Theorem var_1).
fit <- mrn(A, C, Y, W_C, W_Y,
           dist1 = "binom", params1 = list(prob = 0.5),
           dist0 = "binom", params0 = list(prob = 0.2),
           distC = "binom", paramsC = list(prob = 0.7))
fit$variance_type
#> [1] "var_1 (Loewner-max, Bernoulli)"
fit$causal_effects
#>                       effect            key estimate  variance        se
#> 1    Overall CE^O(phi1,phi0)     CE_overall 5.959401 2.1183410 1.4554521
#> 2          Direct CE^D(phi1) CE_direct_phi1 5.066717 2.1529917 1.4673076
#> 3          Direct CE^D(phi0) CE_direct_phi0 4.850573 0.5533077 0.7438466
#> 4 Indirect CE^I(1;phi1,phi0) CE_indirect_w1 4.111063 2.1116946 1.4531671
#> 5 Indirect CE^I(0;phi1,phi0) CE_indirect_w0 3.894918 0.3836304 0.6193790
#> 6      Total CE^T(phi1,phi0)       CE_total 8.961636 2.9628774 1.7213011
#>   well_defined
#> 1         TRUE
#> 2         TRUE
#> 3         TRUE
#> 4         TRUE
#> 5         TRUE
#> 6         TRUE
fit$potential_outcomes
#>       estimand          key estimate  variance        se well_defined
#> 1   Ybar(phi1)    Ybar_phi1 7.207591 1.6561191 1.2869029         TRUE
#> 2   Ybar(phi0)    Ybar_phi0 1.248190 0.6661849 0.8162015         TRUE
#> 3 Ybar(1,phi1) Ybar_w1_phi1 9.180187 2.3992024 1.5489359         TRUE
#> 4 Ybar(0,phi1) Ybar_w0_phi1 4.113469 0.4024912 0.6344219         TRUE
#> 5 Ybar(1,phi0) Ybar_w1_phi0 5.069124 0.4852292 0.6965840         TRUE
#> 6 Ybar(0,phi0) Ybar_w0_phi0 0.218551 0.3056427 0.5528496         TRUE

## Cluster-level complete randomization (exactly 7 of 10 clusters
## treated, distC = "hypergeom"): the bias-corrected variance
## estimator of Section 6.3 is used automatically.
W_C2 <- as.integer(seq_len(K) %in% sample.int(K, 7))
W_Y2 <- rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(W_C2[C] == 1, 0.5, 0.2))
Y2 <- as.vector(-1 + A %*% (2 * W_Y2) +
                  W_Y2 * as.vector(A %*% (1 * W_Y2)) + rnorm(n))
fit_bc <- mrn(A, C, Y2, W_C2, W_Y2,
              params1 = list(prob = 0.5), params0 = list(prob = 0.2),
              distC = "hypergeom", paramsC = list(m = 7))
fit_bc$variance_type
#> [1] "var_1 bias-corrected (complete rand.)"
fit_bc$causal_effects
#>                       effect            key estimate  variance        se
#> 1    Overall CE^O(phi1,phi0)     CE_overall 2.997105 0.5362698 0.7323044
#> 2          Direct CE^D(phi1) CE_direct_phi1 4.383455 0.1773443 0.4211227
#> 3          Direct CE^D(phi0) CE_direct_phi0 2.806703 0.5536457 0.7440737
#> 4 Indirect CE^I(1;phi1,phi0) CE_indirect_w1 3.297785 0.6898760 0.8305878
#> 5 Indirect CE^I(0;phi1,phi0) CE_indirect_w0 1.721033 0.2962016 0.5442440
#> 6      Total CE^T(phi1,phi0)       CE_total 6.104488 0.6063437 0.7786807
#>   well_defined
#> 1         TRUE
#> 2         TRUE
#> 3         TRUE
#> 4         TRUE
#> 5         TRUE
#> 6         TRUE
